description: Each college's size is the number of player_college records it has (player-years).

d.request: Group player_college records by college_id (treating null college_ids as a separate group), count records per group, identify groups with count strictly exceeding the overall mean, and return: the mean count of those above-average groups, the mean of (each above-average group's count divided by the sum of all counts), and the mean of (each above-average group's count minus the overall mean count).
d.sql: WITH grouped AS (SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM player_college GROUP BY college_id), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) as overall_mean, SUM(cnt) as total_count FROM grouped), above_mean_groups AS (SELECT g.cnt, s.overall_mean, s.total_count FROM grouped g, stats s WHERE g.cnt > s.overall_mean) SELECT AVG(cnt) as mean_count, AVG(cnt * 1.0 / total_count) as mean_proportion, AVG(cnt - overall_mean) as mean_difference FROM above_mean_groups

c.request: Using `player_college`, work out each college's player count (by `college_id`, with records lacking a college_id treated as one group). Then find the colleges whose player count is strictly above the average across all colleges. Return a single row with: (1) those colleges' average player count; (2) the average of each one's player count as a fraction of the total of all colleges' player counts; and (3) the average amount by which they exceed the all-college average. Do not round. Each college's size is the number of player_college records it has (player-years).
c.sql:
WITH college_counts AS (
  SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) as player_count
  FROM player_college
  GROUP BY college_id
),
overall_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(player_count) as avg_player_count, SUM(player_count) as total_players
  FROM college_counts
),
above_avg_colleges AS (
  SELECT cc.player_count, os.avg_player_count, os.total_players
  FROM college_counts cc
  CROSS JOIN overall_stats os
  WHERE cc.player_count > os.avg_player_count
)
SELECT 
  AVG(player_count) as avg_count_above_avg,
  AVG(CAST(player_count AS NUMERIC) / total_players) as avg_fraction_of_total,
  AVG(player_count - avg_player_count) as avg_excess_above_mean
FROM above_avg_colleges

a.request: In `player_college`, give each college (by `college_id`, with records lacking a college_id treated as one group) a count equal to its number of records, so every player-year row counts. Find the colleges whose count is strictly above the average count across all colleges. Return a single row with: (1) the average count among those colleges; (2) the average of each such college's count divided by the total of the counts summed over all colleges; and (3) the average amount by which their counts exceed the all-college average count. Do not round.
a.sql:
WITH college_counts AS (
  SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) as cnt
  FROM player_college
  GROUP BY college_id
),
overall_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(CAST(cnt AS FLOAT)) as avg_count,
    SUM(cnt) as total_count
  FROM college_counts
),
above_average_colleges AS (
  SELECT cc.cnt
  FROM college_counts cc
  CROSS JOIN overall_stats os
  WHERE cc.cnt > os.avg_count
)
SELECT
  AVG(CAST(aac.cnt AS FLOAT)) as metric1,
  AVG(CAST(aac.cnt AS FLOAT) / CAST(os.total_count AS FLOAT)) as metric2,
  AVG(CAST(aac.cnt AS FLOAT) - os.avg_count) as metric3
FROM above_average_colleges aac
CROSS JOIN overall_stats os

b.request: Group player_college records by college_id (treating NULL college_id as a single group), count records per group, calculate the mean count across all groups, select groups with count strictly above this mean, and return: (1) the mean record count of selected groups, (2) the mean of each selected group's count divided by the total count across all groups, and (3) the mean difference between each selected group's count and the overall mean count.
b.sql:
WITH grouped_counts AS (
  SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) as group_count
  FROM player_college
  GROUP BY college_id
),
overall_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(group_count) as overall_mean,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_college) as total_count
  FROM grouped_counts
),
selected_groups AS (
  SELECT 
    gc.group_count,
    os.total_count,
    os.overall_mean
  FROM grouped_counts gc
  CROSS JOIN overall_stats os
  WHERE gc.group_count > os.overall_mean
)
SELECT 
  AVG(group_count) as mean_record_count_of_selected_groups,
  AVG(CAST(group_count AS FLOAT) / total_count) as mean_proportion_of_total,
  AVG(group_count - overall_mean) as mean_difference_from_overall_mean
FROM selected_groups
